transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today? How have you been feeling lately?

Well... my wife wanted me to come. I guess... it's about this memorial I'm putting together for my brother. It's just... gotten a bit bigger than I originally planned. I've been spending most of my days on it—tracking down specific songs, making calls, sorting out displays, and planning some trips for it. My wife says I've been... neglecting other things. The garden, my walking group... pretty much everything else, according to her. I'm just trying to get it right.
Do you feel that you have to do these things for the memorial in a certain way, or that something bad might happen if you don't? Or is it more that you just want it to be perfect for your brother?

I don't think anything bad will happen, exactly. It's just... well, it's not just about making it perfect. 

It's... I know how it sounds. But my brother, he had these old ballads he kept. And... I've been listening to them. Really listening. 

I'm... certain they aren't just songs. There are... warnings, I guess you could call them. Tucked into the lyrics. For me. My wife thinks I'm reading too much into it, but... I know what I heard. So I have to get it right.
When you say there are warnings in the lyrics for you, can you tell me more about what you mean? Do you feel these warnings are predicting something specific that could happen to you or others?

Well... I don't really want to get into all the details. It's... it's just things I hear when I listen to them. 

Like I said, I know it sounds odd. My wife thinks I'm crazy, says I'm reading too much into it. But... I know what I heard in those words. They're meant for me. That's... that's all I really want to say about it.
Do you believe that the warnings you hear in the songs are part of some larger hidden message or plot that others don’t understand?

Look, I don't know about any... plots or anything like that. 

Like I already said, I just know those old ballads aren't just regular songs. They've got warnings tucked in them, specifically for me. My wife keeps telling me I'm reading too much into it, but... I know what I heard in those words. 

I'd really rather just leave it at that.
Do you believe that only you can understand these warnings in the songs, even though others, like your wife, don’t hear them the same way?

Yes. I mean... I guess so. 

She just hears the music, the story in the song. But... I hear what's underneath it. I already told you, I know it sounds strange. I know she thinks I'm making it up or... or losing my mind. But I'm not. 

I just... I know what I heard. The warnings are there. They're for me. I don't really want to keep going over this.
Do you think that your understanding of the songs is the only correct one, even though others don’t share that view?

Look... yes. I'm certain of it. 

Those old ballads my brother kept, they just... they aren't just songs. I know it sounds odd to you, too. But they've got warnings tucked in them for me. Even when my wife says I'm reading too much into it, it doesn't change anything. I still know what I heard in those words. 

I've answered this already. I really don't want to keep explaining it.
Has this belief about the songs affected other areas of your life, such as your ability to focus on daily tasks, your relationships, or your mood?

I suppose it has... affected things. 

I haven't been going to my walking group or the book club lately. I just... haven't had the time or the focus. The garden is a mess right now. And I guess I upset some folks down at the senior center because... well, I was talking a lot about the memorial display I'm working on. It's important. 

My wife... she says our whole day is just about trying to calm me down, or stopping me from making another phone call, or taking another trip to get things for it. She says we're always arguing about it now. 

I don't know. I'm just busy with it.
Have you ever had any other beliefs or ideas that you are certain are true, but others around you do not seem to understand or agree with?

No. Just... no. 

Just what we've already been talking about. The songs. I don't have any other... ideas, or whatever you're looking for. Just that. I don't really know what else you mean.
Have you ever had any experiences where you were sure something was real or true, but others told you it wasn’t, and you still believed it even though there was no proof?

I don't... no. I mean, you're asking the same thing again, just using different words. 

I already told you about the songs. There isn't anything else. I just... I don't have anything else to say about it.
Have you ever had any other unusual beliefs or experiences that you were certain were true, even when others told you they weren’t and there was no proof to support them?

Look... I don't know how many different ways you want me to say it. No. 

There's nothing else. Just what we already talked about. I don't... I don't have anything else to tell you about that.
Have you ever experienced things like hearing voices or seeing things that others don’t seem to hear or see?

Well... yeah, I guess. Sometimes. 

When I'm sitting at the kitchen table... sorting through his song sheets. I'll hear him. My brother. His voice is... just right there behind me. Humming, mostly. Or telling me which tune is supposed to come next. 

My wife says it's quiet in the house, but... I hear him. Clear as day.
Do you ever question whether the warnings you hear in the songs might not actually be there, or do you feel completely certain they are real and meant specifically for you?

I don't question it. I know it sounds odd to other people, but... I'm certain. 

Those old ballads he kept, they aren't just songs. There are warnings tucked in them. For me. 

My wife tells me I'm reading too much into it. She says it's just old music. But... I know what I heard in those words. I know what they mean.
